reason: Preserve completed capture results when the other process output stream exceeds its drain deadline, preventing a supervisor panic during SSH or child-process cleanup.
compatibility: Keep command timeout, cancellation, process-tree termination, output limits, successful output and CaptureDrainTimedOut semantics unchanged. A pinned aggregate join owns each completed result exactly once; cleanup aborts and reaps unfinished captures without polling consumed handles again. Cross-platform unit cases and Linux native exit/timeout/cancel regressions remain required; native and Windows CI gates are retained.
